title: Final pilot sync - value synthesis and rollout schedule
next_steps: Redwood to send final pilot summary + cost model (Maya) by 2025-12-05
Customer to confirm go/no-go decision and preferred deployment mode by 2025-12-12
Schedule exec readout with Novus leadership for week of 2025-12-15 (Samir to coordinate)
Jordan to share benchmark run logs and KV cache config notes by 2025-12-04
action_items: Maya (Redwood) - compile one-page ROI slide and send link to pilot-results.xlsx - due 2025-12-05
Jordan (Redwood SE) - export perf traces for 99th percentile latency and attach - due 2025-12-04
Marco (Novus Infra) - provide VPC peering details and firewall rules that blocked initial test - due 2025-12-06
Priya (Novus) - confirm primary success metric (reduction in triage time) and threshold - due 2025-12-10
summary: Final weekly pilot sync focused on aligning stakeholders on measured outcomes and closing the business case. Redwood reviewed pilot metrics, discussed tuning performed (quantization + batching), called out remaining infra blockers, and agreed next steps for commercial review and exec readout. Customer expressed preference for Dedicated if SLA and data residency assurances align; cost model scenarios were requested.
topics: Pilot results recap (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on triage task)
Tuning and config changes performed (int8, KV prefix caching, batch sizes)
Commercial scenarios: hosted vs dedicated vs private
Success criteria and timeline for go/no-go
Next steps and exec readout scheduling
questions: What is the confirmed 99th pct latency under peak (and with cache warm)?
Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS for key rotation?
How does cost change if we move from hosted to dedicated with reserved capacity?
Are audit logs retained in Private deployment for 13 months?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about 55, 60 minutes today, final sync of the pilot. Quick agenda: results recap, tuning recap, infra blockers, and then business case / next steps.
[00:12] Priya: Great, thanks. We have leadership on the line for the last 20 minutes, so hope to land on clear asks.
[00:20] Jordan: Quick heads-up — I'm going to share the pilot-results.xlsx in chat, it's the raw numbers plus the per-route token breakdown.
[00:31] (link posted) pilot-results.xlsx
[00:35] Daniel: I skimmed the sheet. First question: the 99th percentile latency looks like 420ms in the report but when we tested it peaked to 620ms — what's the delta?
[00:45] Jordan: Yeah, good call. The 420ms is with KV cache warm and continuous batching at the observed production qps. The run that hit 620ms was during a synthetic spike with cold cache and hermetic load — not representative of steady state. We do show both warm/cold numbers in the sheet.
[00:58] Marco: We saw several connection resets during that spike — firewall dropped some keepalives, might have contributed. I'll attach the VPC flow logs after.
[01:10] Maya: Perfect, Marco. One of the outcomes here is to quantify the expected tail latency once infra issues are fixed.
[01:22] Priya: From a success criteria POV, our main metric is triage throughput improvement — i.e., time to label critical cases down by 30% and less than 500ms median latency.
[01:35] Lina: Also need to ensure model outputs meet our safety filters, false positive rate below 6% on triage alerts.
[01:45] Jordan: On tuning — we ran int8 quant on the encoder and kept the decoder in int16 for stability. That shaved about 22% off per-token GPU time and didn't degrade the triage classifier score beyond 1.2% delta.
[01:58] Daniel: Can you explain the decision to not fully quantize?
[02:03] Jordan: Sure — we observed inference artifacts when fully quantizing the final layers for this specific model family; decoders were sensitive and produced slightly hallucinated labels in edge cases. So hybrid quant preserved quality.
[02:16] Priya: Okay that's reasonable. How about batching — what batch sizes did you run in the dedicated experiments vs hosted baseline?
[02:25] Jordan: Baseline hosted experiments used dynamic batching with average batch 8, peak 16. Dedicated runs used a more aggressive batch target of 24 with smart-routing to keep latency SLOs. That gave ~15% cost reduction per request.
[02:40] Maya: Note — those numbers assume the prefix caching remains enabled. If the workload has lots of unique prefixes, savings shrink.
[02:51] Lina: Our prefixes are fairly repetitive for the triage flow, so cache hit rates were good in our pilot (~78%).
[03:00] Priya: On security — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS so keys never leave our control?
[03:06] Samir: Short answer yes. We have a customer-managed KMS option in Private and Dedicated flows; we'll share the KMS integration doc. For hosted, we provide HSM-backed keys but not customer-managed.
[03:20] Daniel: What's the difference in cost and SLA if we go Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:25] Maya: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, lower per-token costs under commit, and SLA-backed latency targets. Hosted is more flexible but higher unit cost. We'll attach two pricing scenarios: a 12-month reserved and a committed 6-month burst option.
[03:41] Marco: The first week we saw packet drops because our outbound NAT timeouts were too low; once we adjusted keepalive the resets stopped. That accounts for the early higher tail.
[03:50] Jordan: Good to call that out. We re-ran the 95/99 curves after the infra tweak — see the 'post-infra' tab.
[04:01] (typing)
[04:15] Maya: Ok, business case time — Priya, you said CFO wants to see ROI tied to reduced triage labor. How many FTE hours are we saving per week in the pilot?
[04:26] Priya: Roughly 48 hours per week across the team based on the pilot sampling. Equates to about $4,400/week.
[04:35] Maya: If we take the cost per 1k tokens from the dedicated reserved scenario it's about $X, which yields payback in 7-9 weeks assuming adoption remains. We'll provide a detailed slide.
[04:47] Daniel: We can't disclose exact $X here in the recording, will accept the spreadsheet after.
[04:52] Maya: Understood, will send.
[05:00] Lina: A couple of product questions — did you notice any drift in classifier outputs over the two-week pilot?
[05:08] Jordan: Minimal drift; we ran automatic eval on the gold set daily and saw a max deviation of 0.8% which is within our alerting threshold. We did see one prompt pattern that slipped — we generated a small supplemental prompt normalization rule to handle it.
[05:23] Priya: In terms of compliance, we need audit logs available for 13 months and redaction of PHI in logs — is that supported?
[05:33] Samir: Yes, Private deployments support configurable log retention and redaction hooks. For Dedicated we can enable audit logging with S3 archiving to your account. We'll link the compliance pack.
[05:45] Priya: Great.
[05:48] (10-minute mark)
[06:05] Jordan: Quick technical note — we used continuous KV cache with TTL of 6 hours for sessionized users. That was critical to the 78% cache hit Lina mentioned. When we simulated 100 concurrent sessions with random prefixes the hit rate dropped to ~52%.
[06:22] Marco: Our workload is closer to sessionized, so 6-hour TTL seems fine.
[06:28] Maya: Ok. On risk: primary open items are (1) VPC firewall tweaks (Marco), (2) final cost scenario (Maya), (3) exec readout scheduling (Samir), and (4) confirm success metric threshold (Priya).
[06:40] Priya: That matches our view. One question from leadership — what are the fallback options if Dedicated capacity isn't available in our target region?
[06:49] Jordan: We have automated fallback to a compatible model variant in another region with cross-region caching and routing. Latency will increase modestly but the service remains available. We can also run a hybrid: primary Dedicated in nearest region with overflow to hosted in adjacent region.
[07:04] Daniel: That overflow is acceptable if we have clear SLOs and pricing for overflow traffic.
[07:10] Maya: We'll include overflow pricing in the cost sheet.
[07:16] (15-minute mark)
[07:28] Lina: One last technical ask — can Redwood provide per-token cost broken down by generation vs embedding calls? We use both in pipeline.
[07:35] Jordan: Yes — the pilot sheet has embedding separate; generation dominates cost. We'll annotate the sheet to make it explicit.
[07:42] Priya: For the exec readout, what do you need from us to present a single recommended option?
[07:48] Maya: Ideally: confirmed latency threshold, expected monthly tokens, and preferred data residency requirement. With those we can show three scenarios and an ROI.
[07:57] Priya: We'll confirm by next Friday.
[08:05] Marco: I'll upload the VPC flow logs and the outbound NAT rules; that'll help you reproduce the earlier connection resets.
[08:12] Samir: Thanks Marco.
[08:18] (20-minute mark)
[08:30] Daniel: Regarding SSO and RBAC, our security team requires SCIM provisioning and role-mapping. Is that in place?
[08:36] Samir: Yes we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for user sync in console. For RBAC we have role templates and custom role creation.
[08:45] Daniel: And can we get a SOC 2 Type II report for the hosted environment?
[08:50] Maya: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 report; for Dedicated/Private we can provide audit artifacts and a compliance pack.
[08:58] Priya: Great.
[09:02] (25-minute mark)
[09:15] Maya: Okay, let's walk through the final numbers on slide 3 of the deck I just shared — the one-pager ROI.
[09:23] (slides shared)
[09:28] Maya: The headline: pilot delivered 44% reduction in average triage latency and estimated 48 FTE hours saved weekly. Cost per triage request in dedicated reserved scenario is considerably lower — we'll give exact figures in the sheet.
[09:46] Lina: The quality metrics — precision/recall numbers — look within tolerance, but we want an additional 2-week burn-in for edge cases. Is that a blocker for procurement?
[09:57] Avery (procurement): We can sign a 6-week extension to validate; procurement is okay with short pilot extension if legal signoff is light.
[10:07] Priya: That helps. We still need the contract language around data usage — no model training, no retention beyond X days.
[10:15] Maya: We'll provide standard data processing addendum (DPA) with clear no-training clause for your pilot.
[10:22] Daniel: What about cost sensitivity — if usage spikes beyond committed tokens, how are we billed?
[10:28] Maya: We provide overage rates, and also burst capacity options for dedicated pools. The pricing sheet includes overage tiers.
[10:34] Daniel: Okay.
[10:36] (30-minute mark)
[10:50] Jordan: One more technical note — for the triage chain we used function-calling to sanitize outputs into structured labels; that decreased downstream parsing errors by 12%.
[10:59] Priya: Nice.
[11:03] Lina: Any known limitations for our multi-tenant dataset mixing? We can't allow cross-tenant leakage.
[11:09] Samir: No cross-tenant leakage in Dedicated; Private even more isolated. We run strict namespacing for KV caches and prompt storage.
[11:18] Marco: For on-prem Private option, do you have an appliance or only AMI images?
[11:24] Jordan: We provide a deployable package with container images and orchestration scripts; for air-gapped installs we have a separate bundle. We'll share the private-deploy README.
[11:33] Priya: Could be useful, but for now Dedicated with VPC peering is our likely path.
[11:40] Maya: Sounds like we have a tentative preference: Dedicated with reserved capacity and overflow to hosted.
[11:48] Daniel: Conditional on SLA numbers and KMS integration.
[11:53] Maya: We'll include a KMS integration plan and SLA targets in the package.
[11:59] (40-minute mark)
[12:10] Maya: Let's capture next steps for exec. Samir will organize a 30-min slot; Redwood will present headline ROI and cost scenarios; Novus will present desired success criteria and legal constraints.
[12:25] Samir: I'll send a Doodle for week of 2025-12-15.
[12:31] Priya: We're good with that.
[12:35] (45-minute mark)
[12:50] Jordan: Minor thing — we noticed a prompt normalization that improved precision. If Novus wants, we can commit a small ruleset to the repo under the pilot namespace.
[12:58] Lina: Yes please, that would help adoption and reduce edge-case errors.
[13:05] Maya: I'll add that to the action items.
[13:12] (50-minute mark)
[13:25] Priya: Final question: what does the formal handover look like if we go to production? Who owns the runbooks?
[13:33] Maya: Redwood provides runbooks, SLO docs, and an onboarding plan. Ownership is typically joint for the first 90 days. After that operational handoff to whoever owns the Dedicated pool (Novus infra or Redwood-managed) per the contract.
[13:49] Daniel: We prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated for the first 6 months.
[13:55] Maya: Noted. We'll include that option in the commercial scenario.
[14:00] Priya: Thanks everyone, we appreciate the clarity. Anything else urgent?
[14:07] Marco: I'll upload flow logs within 24 hours.
[14:12] Maya: Great. We'll send the single-page ROI + pricing scenarios by Friday. Samir will schedule exec readout. Jordan will push the perf traces.
[14:24] (call close)
[14:30] Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.
timestamped_length_estimate: ~14 minutes of transcript shown; call duration 58 minutes — rest was Q&A and exec scheduling at end
